content:
Recurring Inter Account Transfer

Set up recurring transfers between bank and cash accounts.

Useful for regular transfers like monthly cash floats or scheduled account sweeps.

Next issue date

The date when the next inter account transfer will be automatically created. This date advances automatically based on your frequency settings.

Set this to the date of your first scheduled transfer. The system checks daily for transfers due to be created.

Interval

The frequency interval for creating transfers. This number works with the period type to set your transfer schedule.

Common examples: 1 Week = weekly transfers, 1 Month = monthly transfers, 3 Months = quarterly movements.

PeriodType

The period type that works with the interval to determine frequency. Select the unit of time for your transfer cycle.

Choose based on how often you need to move money between accounts.

MonthDay

For monthly recurring transfers, specify which day of the month the transfer should occur.

Useful for scheduling transfers to coincide with specific dates like salary deposits or bill payments.

ExpirationType

Determines when the recurring schedule ends. This controls how long the system will continue creating transfers.

Choose 'Until further notice' for indefinite transfers like regular savings, or 'Until date' for transfers with a known end point.

UntilDate

The date when recurring transfers will stop being created. The system will not create any transfers after this date.

Use this for transfers related to loans with fixed end dates or temporary cash management needs.

Description

A description that identifies this recurring transfer and will be copied to each generated transfer.

Be descriptive to help track money movements. Examples: 'Weekly petty cash top-up', 'Monthly savings deposit', 'Loan repayment transfer'.

Paid from

The bank or cash account from which money will be transferred. This account's balance will decrease by the transfer amount.

Select the account that has the funds to transfer. This could be your main operating account or any account with surplus funds.

CreditAmount

The amount to transfer from the source account in its currency.

Enter the exact amount to transfer each time. This amount will be deducted from the source account.

CreditClearStatus

The clearing status for the source account transaction. Controls how the transfer appears in bank reconciliation.

Use 'Pending' for transfers that need to clear through the banking system, or 'Cleared' for internal transfers.

Received in

The bank or cash account that will receive the transferred money. This account's balance will increase by the transfer amount.

Select the destination account. This could be a savings account, loan account, or any account receiving the funds.

DebitAmount

The amount to receive in the destination account. Only shown when transferring between accounts with different currencies.

For foreign currency transfers, enter the amount in the destination account's currency after exchange rate conversion.

DebitClearStatus

The clearing status for the destination account transaction. Controls how the transfer appears in bank reconciliation.

Usually matches the source account clearing status, but can differ for transfers between different bank institutions.

Automatic reference

When enabled, the system automatically assigns sequential reference numbers to each generated transfer.

Recommended for tracking transfers systematically. The reference helps identify transfers in bank statements.
